evidence: Cic. de Or. 3.216 (Lewis & Short: “a voice, sound, tone”)
terms.comment: Latin speaks of the voice itself, which takes on the colour of each feeling (Cic. de Or. 3.216–219); it also means a word, a saying, a language, and an accent (rūstica vōx et agrestis, de Or. 3.42).

terms.gloss: the sound of a voice; tone, character
evidence: Gell. 13.20.12: sonus vōcis (Lewis & Short, s.v. injūcundus)
Cic. Opt. Gen. 1: suus est cuique certus sonus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A sound or noise, and in Cicero the tone or style of a speech or a genre.

terms.gloss: a kind of voice, a tone
evidence: Cic. de Or. 3.217: vōcis genus crēbrō incīdēns (Lewis & Short, s.v. incīdō)
terms.comment: Cicero’s phrase for the tone a speaker takes for each feeling: here a voice broken by sobs.

phrases.latin: nunc ego tibi īrāscī videor? ex vultūne meō an ex vōce an ex colōre an etiam ex verbīs correptum esse mē īrā intellegis?
phrases.english: do I seem angry to you now? Is it from my face, or my tone, or my colour, or my words that you gather I am in the grip of anger?

phrases.latin: et in cēterīs suus est cuique certus sonus
phrases.english: and in the other kinds each has its own fixed tone
